hero.deck: I investigate how molecular interfaces, defects, and electronic and ionic dynamics govern transport, memory-state formation, variability, and reliability. My work connects physical mechanisms with experimental devices across memory, optoelectronic, and thin-film platforms.
hero.focusFuture: Emerging memory · Thin-film electronics · Integrated systems
hero.affiliation: Integrated M.S.–Ph.D. researcher · School of Electrical Engineering, Korea University

research.title: Research
research.foundationText: Organic and hybrid optoelectronics and printed electronics form connected foundations for this device-physics research.

breadth.title: Research breadth
breadth.intro: Connected work in molecular contacts, thin-film electrodes, and printed electronics extends the same mechanism-driven approach across device platforms.

areas.title: Molecular Interfaces & Thin-Film Electrodes
areas.description: Contact energetics, charge-selective molecular interfaces, and ALD-based electrode platforms for photovoltaic and capacitor devices.

areas.title: Printed & Flexible Electronics
areas.description: Process-induced thickness variation, trace-to-trace electrical nonuniformity, and resistance changes under repeated deformation.

about.title: About
about.text: Min Jong Lee is an integrated M.S.–Ph.D. researcher in electrical engineering at Korea University. His first-author work connects molecular interfaces, optoelectronic devices, and emerging memory.
